craft_claim: No study isolates cynical prose tone, so saturation guidance is inferred: adjacent findings on aggressive-humor costs, detected persuasion intent, and the correlates of chronic distrust imply that unrecovered irony habituates and must yield at intervals.

supporting_evidence.note: If aggressive, ridiculing humor as a sustained style tracks poorer relational outcomes, then a text that sustains barbed irony without relief accumulates the same tax in the reader-writer relation.
Readers monitor for the performing agent's intent; once the deflating voice is read as a stance being performed on them, each further deflation lands with less recognition and more irritation.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 110(1):116-132
supporting_evidence.note: Chronic distrust is documented as costly rather than costless; prose that offers the reader no release from distrust models a disposition that burdens rather than frees. The mapping to reader fatigue is analogical.

counterevidence.note: Persuasion knowledge equips people to cope in varied ways, compliance included; detecting a performing or persuasive agent does not automatically produce backlash, so irony's budget is wide for readers who enjoy the game.

scope: Long-form and serial content; feeds card section 4. Honest null: no direct tone-isolation dosage study was found.
exceptions: Short forms (a single satirical essay or epigram sequence) may sustain deflation to the last line because the form ends before habituation.
Deadpan delivery can carry sustained irony farther than barbed asides because it lowers the hostile signal.
